During contact cycles the sheet temperature increases to a peak followed by cooling and evaporation. The application of RF minimizes this cooling of the sheet; however, the application of US allows the sheet to continue to cool due to lack of thermal energy dissipation during ultrasonic application. It should be noted that the experimental sheet temperature is an average of two thermocouples embedded in the sheet while the simulated temperature is a true average across the whole sheet thickness, hence contributing to the differences in magnitude between the two. 32 DE-EE0009395 Figure 24. Comparison between experimental data and modeling results for sheet temperature vs time during optimal integration of RFUS during multi-cylinder drying (RF 500W 2s and 120W US 1s) Both the experimental data and modeling results showed a similar greater than 30% improvement in drying rate and drying time. Similar results were obtained for other cases of RFUS integration with higher wattages of RF and changing application times. Figures 25 and 26 show the drying rate vs drying time or cylinder number for two different cases of RFUS integration with multi-cylinder drying. The labels contact drying, pure convection and RF (plus convection) in Figures 25 and 26 refer to subsequent periods of contact drying with the cylinder, pure convection in the pockets, and RF+convection as the sheet is dried on the paper machine. In each case, it is clear that RFUS integration gives higher instantaneous drying rates, longer constant drying rate period and shorter falling rate period compared to the base case multi-cylinder drying. These results confirm with experimental data demonstrating the benefits of RFUS with uniform volumetric heating and water removal resulting in increased drying rates during the entire drying periods including the falling rate period and shorter falling rate period. 33 DE-EE0009395 Figure 25. Comparison of drying rate vs time (or cylinder number) between base case multi cylinder drying and another RFUS integration. Based on experimental data and modeling and simulation results, we have shown that with optimal integration of the RFUS, we can achieve greater than 30% improvements in drying rates compared to the base case conduction and convection, reaching the minimum and stretch target improvements in overall drying rates. Benefits Assessment The techno-economic analysis (TEA) and environmental Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) evaluating the RFUS drying of paper and board in conjunction with commercial multi cylinder drying was conducted based on technical modeling, experimental data and input from industry and literature. Techno-Economic Analysis (TEA) The DOE Energy Bandwidth Study of 2006 and also the 2015 update were reviewed. Detailed conversations with industry representatives (APPTI) were performed to accommodate the impact on the balance of plant alterations to paper drying processes.
